title: Безопасное удаление тем: авто-восстановление вместо падения
why: Ручное удаление темы в Telegram молча ломало диалог клиенту: узел «Telegram — отразить сообщение клиента» падал с «message thread not found», а он — жёсткие ворота перед всей цепочкой ответа, и агент до ответа не доходил. thread_for_lead() при этом вечно возвращал мёртвый topic_id, так что клиент оставался без ответа навсегда.
description: У узла-зеркала включён аварийный выход (continueErrorOutput). Он ведёт в «Тема — восстановление?» (защита от петли: $runIndex === 0) -> «Тема — битая: закрыть» (PATCH handoff_threads в closed; частичный уникальный индекс требует закрыть ДО вставки новой) -> существующая цепочка создания темы -> повторная отправка зеркала. При второй неудаче — мягкий выход прямо в IF Spam, клиент в любом случае получает ответ. «Тема — свести topicId» теперь предпочитает тему, созданную в этом же прогоне (иначе повтор подставлял ту же мёртвую); «Хендофф — записать тему» переведён с .item на .first()/.last(), чтобы не зависеть от paired-item на аварийном пути.

title: Web widget: real unread badge while the panel is closed
why: Roadmap block 1: a manager's reply never reached a visitor who had closed the panel. schedule()/poll() bailed out entirely once opened became false, so nothing polled again until the panel was reopened -- the main sales path was silently dropping replies.
description: widget/gaudi-chat.js: schedule()/poll() now key off started + document.hidden instead of opened, running a slow 25s background poll while the page is open and the panel is closed; close() calls schedule() again so the loop keeps running instead of going silent. A bot/manager message arriving while closed calls the new markUnread(): adds .unread to the launcher (CSS lets .newdot win over .calm) and reuses the pre-chat teaser bubble to show a plain-text preview with the sender's name (new plainPreview()/dismissReplyTeaser() helpers, teaserMode flag). Opening the panel clears the badge and the bubble and shows the message, already appended to the thread from the background fetch. Teaser click handling moved out from under 'if (INVITE_ON)' so the preview bubble stays clickable on sites that disable the marketing invite. No backend change: the poll: throttle bucket (600 req/10min per IP) has headroom for the added background requests.
test: ПРОВЕРЕНО ВЖИВУЮ 2026-09-04 — Live-tested on gaudidecor.eu via the built-in browser pane (2026-09-04): sent a message through the widget, closed the panel, then wrote a role='manager' row into messages directly (bypassing Telegram) to isolate the widget's own logic. Confirmed document.hidden correctly pauses the background poll while the pane/tab is not visible, and resumes it (visibilitychange -> poll()) once visible again. Within one 25s background cycle after becoming visible: launcher gained class unread (dot shows through .calm via the new CSS rule), the teaser bubble showed the manager's name and a plain-text preview of the message, and the reply was already appended to the thread. Clicking the launcher cleared both unread and the bubble and opened the panel with the message already there. Did not separately live-test the data-invite=off code path (teaser click handler moved outside the INVITE_ON guard) or a real Telegram-manager round trip -- both are low-risk, mechanical changes.

title: Manager pause: an exact per-message timer instead of 5-minute polling
why: Releasing the manager pause rested on a Schedule Trigger every 5 minutes: ~8600 executions a month before a single client, and up to 5 minutes late. Checked while redesigning: human_since IS already rewritten on every manager message (the write hangs off 'Хендофф — команда /release?' out1 in parallel with the IF, not behind it), so the hour was already counted from the manager's LAST message - the only real inaccuracy was the polling lag.
description: New branch off 'Хендофф — пауза: записать': Wait node 'Хендофф — пауза: таймер' (60 min) -> 'Хендофф — таймер: сессия' (GET the session row) -> 'Хендофф — таймер: решение' (Code). The wait lives inside the manager-message execution, so it creates no extra executions. Because every manager message starts its own timer, the decision node releases only if human_active is still true AND human_since is at least 59.5 min old - a later message makes an earlier timer exit silently and the last one does the release. It feeds the existing auto-release chain by emitting a session-shaped row into 'Хендофф — тайм-аут: список сессий', so nothing downstream had to be duplicated. Schedule Trigger dropped from every 5 minutes to every 12 hours and demoted to a safety net for waits lost to a workflow rewrite (deploy.py rewrites the workflow several times a session). Manager reminder text now says 'через час после вашего последнего сообщения' instead of 'через 60 минут', matching what actually happens.

title: Build scripts: stamp-only redeploy, and a --no-test release option
why: Two friction points found while shipping v5.44. (1) deploy.py returned early whenever rule text matched, so after a version bump that changed no rule text the live prompt kept the old stamp forever and every later --check printed a false 'not redeployed after bump' warning. (2) release.py forced either --test or --test-todo, so a typo-level fix still queued a live test run; Artyom's call: a live check that costs more than the fix itself should not be mandatory.
description: deploy.py: the no-drift early return now also checks stale version stamps, and redeploys stamp-only when rule text is identical. release.py: new --no-test REASON, mutually exclusive with --test/--test-todo, writing 'Тест: НЕ ТРЕБУЕТСЯ — reason' into the CHANGELOG. The prefix is deliberately different from the one state_check.py watches, so such entries never show up as a pending live-test tail. Exactly one of the three flags is still required - the point was never to allow silence about testing, only to stop forcing a run that is not worth it.

title: search_catalog: zero-result queries broke the tool call
why: Live-tested M-68 (article-not-found wording): search_catalog for a nonexistent article code errored with n8n's 'workflow did not return a response' instead of a clean empty result. Root cause found via execution 1313: pool_select.js (node 'Каталог — пул', last node in the search_catalog sub-workflow) returned an EMPTY items array on zero matches (rows.map() over []); the AI-tool wrapper treats zero output items as no response at all, not a valid empty answer. This breaks ANY search_catalog call with zero matches, not just article lookups by code — likely the real cause behind other 'catalogue not responding' reports too.
description: pool_select.js: zero-match branch now returns exactly one item {total_found:0, total_capped:false} instead of an empty array, so the tool call always gets a real response and the agent can follow M-68/M-59 wording correctly instead of improvising.
